Email remains visible in person cards and command feedback while the
field is being phased out.

Remove it from the person card and formatted command messages. Add a
focused regression test for the remaining user-facing message fields.

Email should no longer be modifiable while the field is being phased
out.

Remove it from the edit command, descriptor, parser, and test utilities.
Reject legacy email edit arguments explicitly. Preserve stored email values
when other fields are edited.

Person records still store email even though it is no longer displayed or
editable.

Remove email from the person model, add command, storage, sample data,
fixtures, and test builders. Reject legacy email command arguments while
continuing to ignore email properties in older JSON files.

The email value object and parser utility are no longer used after email
was removed from person records.

Delete the obsolete model class, parser method, and their tests. Keep the
legacy email prefix so add and edit commands can reject old input clearly.

The user and developer guides still describe email as part of a person
after the field was removed from the application.

Update add and edit command examples, and regenerate the model diagrams
without the obsolete Email class and relationship.
Remove address support from Person
Resolve overlapping Person, storage, UI, test, and documentation changes while removing Email and Address and retaining Score.
Exercise sample Person construction and the hash code contract so the email-removal patch remains covered by Codecov.

Members can record incorrect orders, but the app has no way to remove
them from an order history.

Add the delete-order command to remove an order by member and order
index while preserving immutable order histories.

Validate invalid input and indexes, and update parser routing, tests,
and user and developer documentation to match the new behavior.

Implements #70.

Milestone rewards need a stable identity before collection, command,
redemption, and UI work can proceed independently.

- Add immutable milestones identified by case-sensitive codes.
- Validate nonblank reward descriptions and positive required scores.
- Cover construction, validation, identity, equality, and formatting.

Part of #88

Milestone rewards need a shared collection that preserves unique
identities and provides a predictable display order.

- Reject null, missing, duplicate, and identity-changing operations.
- Sort milestones by required score and code after mutations.
- Expose an observable read-only view for later UI integration.
- Test ordering, defensive behavior, notifications, and iteration.

Part of #88

Milestone rewards are global programme data and need to remain
consistent with member records during model copies and resets.

- Add milestone operations and read-only access to the address book.
- Include milestones in copies, equality, hashing, and diagnostics.
- Validate replacement data before applying either address book list.
- Test mutations, ordering, defensive access, and atomic resets.

Part of #88

Milestone commands need a stable Model API so command and UI work can
use rewards without depending on AddressBook internals.

- Add milestone query, add, edit, delete, and list operations to Model.
- Delegate milestone operations through ModelManager.
- Keep the exposed milestone list observable and unmodifiable.
- Cover model behavior and update the existing test stub.

Part of #88

Milestone UI work needs read-only access to the model's live reward
list without crossing the Logic boundary.

- Add milestone list access to Logic and LogicManager.
- Preserve observable updates while preventing external mutations.
- Test live updates and read-only access.

Part of #88

commitResults.messageBody:
Milestones need to survive restarts and reject malformed saved data at
the storage boundary.

- Add a Jackson adapter with missing-field and constraint validation.
- Serialize and restore milestones alongside persons.
- Accept legacy files that do not contain a milestones field.
- Reject duplicate milestone codes during model conversion.
- Cover validation and round-trip storage in milestone-specific tests.

Part of #88
Allow stall owners to add menu items with a unique code, name and price

Upstream master now contains the menu-item feature from #96. The
milestone branch extends several of the same model contracts and tests.

- Preserve both menu and milestone APIs in the integrated model.
- Keep the menu persistence and milestone observation test coverage.
- Update the menu command test stub for the combined Model contract.
- Verify the integrated code with the full Gradle check.

Integrates upstream changes from #96 with work for #88.

Milestone codes identify rewards across the model and persistence.
Case variants should not create distinct reward identities.

Normalize valid codes to uppercase and reject case-only duplicates.
Add model, collection, and storage regression tests.

Milestones are global loyalty-program configuration, but the existing
collection has no aggregate separate from AddressBook.

Introduce MilestoneCatalog and ReadOnlyMilestoneCatalog to own milestone
operations behind a focused model boundary. Add tests for copying,
validation, sorting, observable views, and value semantics.

This prepares milestones to become an independent data source without
changing the current application wiring.

Milestone catalogs need their own persistence boundary before they can
be wired into the application.

Add JSON serialization and file storage for independent catalogs.
Validate malformed structures, duplicate codes, and invalid fields.

Reject JSON type coercion for milestone fields so persisted scores and
identifiers cannot change meaning while loading.

Milestones are global loyalty-program configuration, but AddressBook
currently owns and persists them alongside member records.

Move milestone ownership to ModelManager and load/save catalogs through
dedicated storage. Keep existing Model and Logic milestone operations
stable while adding a read-only catalog accessor for persistence.

Ignore legacy milestone fields in memberlist data instead of migrating
them because the feature has not been released.

Update model, startup, storage, and logic tests to cover independent
loading, saving, failure handling, and restart behavior.

Milestones now live outside the address book, so the guides need to
reflect the new data boundary.

Document milestones.json, validation, startup fallback, and save
behavior. Update backup guidance to include all independent domain data
files.

Explain catalog ownership and persistence without changing architecture
diagrams maintained under a separate team task.

ModelManager and StorageManager now coordinate milestone catalog data,
but their class descriptions still list only the older data sources.

Update both descriptions so they accurately reflect each manager's
current responsibilities.

Milestone loading failures are logged without their exception objects,
so the resulting logs omit stack traces needed for diagnosis.

Pass the exceptions to the storage and startup log records while
preserving their existing severity and fallback behavior.

Milestones can be managed through the model but cannot be created
through the command interface.

Add an add-milestone command with code, reward, and required-score
arguments. Validate the complete input before adding the milestone and
preserve the catalog's case-insensitive code identity.

Milestone details cannot be changed through the command interface.

Add an edit-milestone command that resolves a displayed index to its
stable milestone identity. Allow the reward or required score to be
updated while keeping milestone codes immutable.

Milestones cannot be removed through the command interface.

Add a delete-milestone command that resolves a displayed index against
the milestone list before deleting the corresponding catalog entry.
Keep redemption records and member scores outside this command's scope.

The user and developer documentation does not describe milestone
management through the command interface.

Document the add, edit, and delete milestone commands, including their
input constraints, displayed-index behavior, sorting effects, and
representative test cases.

Index-based milestone commands require a visible, authoritative list so
users can identify their targets.

Add list-milestones to display numbered rewards in model order. Document
the output, sorting contract, and manual tests for empty and populated
catalogs.
